chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel that exists in front of the K

1.original: [of the King of Honour who dwells in]
1.content: of the King of Honour who dwells in

fills.notes: The oldest-layer register avoids personal citation; the clause needs an impersonal subject: “the teaching speaks about the wheel…”.

fills.fill: of the King of Honour who dwells in
fills.notes: Fits the cosmological locating of the Wheel before the enthroned King in the 7th firmament; no better constraint from context.

The phrase after “seventh firmament” requires a locative completion in the same cosmological style; “in the height” maintains impersonal substrate diction (upper region) rather than later devotional expansions.
Parallelism: enmity in the firmaments is ‘gathered and ensnared’ in the Wheel, matching the fetter/containment logic and the later ‘root… ensnared and fixed’.
The seal functions as a boundary-lock between each firmament and its archontic occupants; “rulers” is demanded by the repeated concern with their attempted escape.
The sentence requires the location of binding: the would-be escapee is bound “in it” (i.e., in the Wheel/fetter).
The apodosis needs a simple disclosure verb: any trick ‘will be apparent and known’.
Completes the disclosure mechanism: what is attempted becomes known ‘immediately’ in the Wheel, consistent with the mirror/manifestation theme in ¶6.

The clause needs the object of ‘observation’: the ‘observation of the wheel’ (i.e., its constant display/disclosure) is set opposite the King, matching the mirror logic and the later ‘recognised and revealed by that wheel’.
The syntax demands continuation into purpose: it is set opposite the King “so that fear…”; keeps to structural causality rather than exhortation.
Fear is defined as something stationed/opposed before the King; “placed there” coheres with the repeated ‘placed in it / set opposite’.
The clause needs a verb for what fear does to the powers of mixture: it ‘assumes’/takes hold; “and seize” tightens the fetter imagery (capture).
Analogy requires a concrete instance: like a chain before a chief guard—when someone tries to flee, he is detected ‘in those (links)’.

fills.fill: ose who are bound, he is recognised
fills.notes: Carries the chain-analogy forward: among ‘those who are bound’ the escapee is identified; keeps impersonal, administrative-cosmological tone.
Mid-word fragment indicates ‘chain’; the surrounding text already resumes with ‘in the … in the …in’. Best restoration is to complete the word-form already implied.
Completes: “the discrimination of all things … is in it” → “is also in it,” reinforcing the Wheel as universal differentiator/manifestation (mirror).

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the chapter’s correspondential mechanics: the Wheel functions as fetter + mirror (binding and disclosure), so restorations cluster around ‘gathering/ensnaring’, ‘recognition/revelation’, and constant ‘placement/opposition’ before the King in the seventh firmament. A few places (¶4–¶5) remain only moderately/ tentatively recoverable because the surviving syntax is thin, but the underlying logic (fear/guard-chain analogy) keeps the restorations within the oldest cosmological register.
